data.title: CoreWeave sinks 12% as tech stocks plunge
data.description:
AI cloud provider CoreWeave (CRWV) slumped just over 12% on Friday as technology shares sold off broadly. The stock finished at $39.46, down $5.45 on the day. Shares also reached a new 52-week low of $39.28.

The XLK technology sector ETF dropped just over 7%, while the QQQ and SPY ETFs lost just over 5% and just over 3%. Peers NVDA, AMD and AVGO fell almost 14%, just over 13% and just over 12%, respectively.

data.title: Monolithic Power Systems retreats 12%, weighed down by tech selloff
data.description:

The decline coincided with a broad market pullback and a steep drop in technology shares. SPY slid just over 3% and QQQ dropped just over 5%, while the technology sector ETF XLK lost just over 7%. Semiconductor peers AMAT, KLAC and MRVL each fell more than 10%.

data.title: Automakers sue NJ over vehicle warranty and recall repair law - Reuters
data.description:
Ford (F), Honda (HMC), Volkswagen (VWAGY) (VWAPY), and Stellantis’ FCA unit (STLA)  are suing New Jersey in an attempt to block a 7-month-old law that leaves automakers responsible for warranty and recall costs.

According to Reuters, the automakers claim the New Jersey Motor Vehicle Open Recall Notice and Fair Compensation Act gives franchised dealerships “unilateral and unchecked power” to charge “extortionate” prices for repairs that automakers are responsible for.  Manufacturers also argue that the statute prevents them from avoiding or recovering the added costs. 

The New Jersey Motor Vehicle Open Recall Notice and Fair Compensation Act requires automakers to pay dealers at least 1.5% of a used vehicle’s value per month if recall parts are unavailable within 30 days of a stop-sale or do-not-drive notice until parts arrive or the vehicle is sold.

The law also sets rules for how automakers reimburse dealers for warranty and recall repairs, including labor rates, prices for parts, labor hours, and claim processing.  

If the automakers are successful in their challenge, it would limit the reach of the current payment system for dealerships in the state. If the challenge fails, the plaintiffs claim the law gives dealers too much control over repair reimbursement.

data.title: Zscaler soars on report CrowdStrike in talks to purchase
data.description:
Zscaler (ZS) jumped 18% on a report that CrowdStrike (CRWD) is in talks to acquire the cybersecurity company. CrowdStrike fell 11%.

The two companies are discussing a potential deal that could come together soon, according to a Bloomberg report on Friday, which cited people familiar with the matter.

Deliberations are ongoing, and there’s no certainty a deal will happen, Bloomberg reported.  Crowdstrike (CRWD) has a market cap of $250 billion, while Zscaler (ZS) is valued at $34 billion.

Representatives for CrowdStrike and Zscaler didn’t immediately respond to requests for comment from Bloomberg.

data.title: Tech stocks lead Wall Street bloodbath as S&P 500 posts massive weekly loss
data.description:
Wall Street’s major averages plummeted lower on Friday and finished deep in the red as the tech selloff intensified.

The blue-chip Dow closed 1.9% lower, the benchmark S&P 500 (SP500) slipped 3.6%, and the tech-focused Nasdaq Composite tumbled 5.2%.

The S&P 500 declined 8.61% for the week.

Seeking Alpha analyst Agar Capital stated that it is clear investor sentiment has shifted this week, and it is not just about the technology sector. As we've seen, until a few weeks ago, the market was selling technology to buy healthcare, consumer staples, and companies considered more defensive. This was a normal sector rotation, driven by nervousness and the news surrounding the AI sector. But when even sectors that until yesterday represented a safe haven start to decline, I think it's necessary to ask a few more questions.

“Nvidia posted extraordinary results, and Anthropic made its stock market debut with a record IPO. Two events that, under normal conditions, could have supported the market. Yet, they didn't. I believe investors are wondering how much risk they're willing to take in this market phase. After all, after four years of a bull market, it's a fair question to ask. I do not feel it is time for us to draw conclusions. There are some excellent underlying fundamentals in many businesses, and corrections often provide an excellent opportunity. However, the distinction between selling out of one area to invest in another versus beginning to sell off assets across the board is what I am concerned about now,” Agar Capital concluded.

From a sector-level perspective, all 11 S&P 500 sectors ended the week in negative territory.

Technology (XLK) and Communication Services (XLC) were the biggest detractors, slipping 10.35% and 6.67%, respectively.

On the other hand, Consumer Staples (XLP) and Utilities (XLU) posted the smallest weekly losses, declining 2% and 3%, respectively.

Seeking Alpha analyst Jack Bowman highlighted that this week was a big risk-off week, and that's super clear in the markets, with the most volatile sectors like tech taking the hardest hit. There was hope that the Anthropic (ANT) IPO would turn things around at the end of the week, but that doesn't seem to be the case so far, although I wouldn't discount it just yet, as it's still too new to say.

“Defensive sectors like staples and utilities did not perform as well as I had expected this week, although they're still certainly benefiting from the risk-off market we're currently in. I expect their relative strength to persist as long as the tech sector is down,” Bowman concluded.

data.title: 3 things investors will look out for on Monday
data.description:
Wall Street’s major averages dove deep into red territory, with the S&P 500 (SP500) and the Dow (DJI) closing in correction territory, and the Nasdaq Composite (COMP:IND) turning negative for the year.

The benchmark S&P 500 (SP500) closed -3.7%, while the tech-heavy Nasdaq (COMP:IND) closed -5.28%, and the blue-chip Dow (DJI) finished -1.94%.

Now, here are three things investors will look out for on Monday:

  • Several large-cap companies are expected to report earnings after Monday’s market close, including Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE), Agilent Technologies (A), Zoom Communications (ZM), and Symbotic (SYM), among others.
  • On the economic calendar, traders will receive the U.S. Flash Manufacturing and Services PMI Index for November. The October print showed an increase to 56.0, up from 55.9 the month prior, a 53-month high.
  • Semiconductor stocks continue to suffer and position themselves among the indexes’ top decliners. Both the S&P 500 (SP500) and the Dow (DJI) are in correction territory, and the Nasdaq Composite (COMP:IND) has erased its 2026 gains entirely. Investors will continue to monitor the AI trade, which many analysts believe is in a bubble.

data.title: SA analyst: Volatility could fade, but markets must stabilize first
data.description:
Wall Street endured a steep selloff Friday, with technology stocks leading a broad market retreat that left major indexes facing one of their worst weekly performances in quite some time.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJI) fell -1.9%, while the S&P 500 (SP500) dropped -3.6% and the Nasdaq Composite (COMP:IND) plunged -5.2%. 

Seeking Alpha analyst Alex King of Cestrian Capital Research acknowledged the difficult stretch for bullish investors but suggested several factors could help markets stabilize in the coming week. 

King pointed to the possibility that the CBOE Volatility Index’s recent spike could quickly reverse, while declining Treasury yields may signal improving conditions for equities. He also cited monthly options expiration as a potential contributor to Friday’s market turbulence. 

“This last week has tested the patience, and likely the resources, of the most zoomed-out bulls,” King stated. However, he cautioned against assuming the worst is over, emphasizing that market price action remains the most important signal. 

“But as always the only thing that matters is price; and price has yet to stabilize in the indices,” he added. King noted that falling yields have supported his bullish outlook on bonds, even as equity markets continue to struggle.

data.title: Sony pulls out of talks with Tishman Speyer on leasing anchor space at new skyscraper - report
data.description:
Sony Group (SONY) (SONY:CA) (SNEJF) has pulled out of negotiations to become an anchor tenant at a new skyscraper in New York City's Hudson Yards, people familiar with the matter told Bloomberg News.

Sony was in talks for a lease with the real estate developer Tishman Speyer as recently as last month, a recent report by the Commercial Observer had noted.

Tishman Speyer is now left without a lease for an anchor space while approaching the final stages of receiving an approval for a key tax break, said the sources, who asked not to be named discussing private negotiations.

data.title: Nasdaq plummets more than -5% and the S&P 500 ends in correction territory
data.description:
Wall Street’s major averages plummeted lower on Friday and finished deep in the red as the tech selloff intensified. 

The blue-chip Dow (DJI) finished -1.9%, the benchmark S&P 500 (SP500) closed -3.6%, and the tech-focused Nasdaq Composite (COMP:IND) ended -5.2%. 

From a sector-by-sector basis, 10 of the 11 segments concluded lower, with info tech leading the way down, while consumer staples was the strongest area.

“This last week has tested the patience, and likely the resources, of the most zoomed-out bulls.  Since the entire Internet is filled with victory laps from bears and cope from bulls, for now I think we can just say; likely the VIX spike collapses next week, likely the drop in yields today portends coming strength in equities, and likely monthly opex today has added to the witches’ brew," Seeking Alpha analyst Alex King of Cestrian Capital Research stated.

Sentiment toward artificial intelligence stocks remained under heavy pressure after Anthropic's (ANT) much-anticipated public market debut failed to provide the boost investors had hoped for, extending a volatile week for equities. 

The U.S. 2-year Treasury yield (US2Y) dropped 13 basis points to 4.63%, the U.S. 10-year Treasury yield (US10Y) shifted down 12 basis points to 4.92%, and the U.S. 30-year Treasury yield (US30Y) moved down 9 basis points to 5.31%. 

As for other stocks that were on the move, shares of Fair Isaac Corp. (FICO) advanced +2.5%, while shares of Sandisk (SNDK) dropped -15.9%.
